---
description: "How NCodeGroup C# code allocates, rents, owns, copies, clears and disposes buffers, strings, collections and disposable resources, so it avoids needless heap allocations and never leaves secret material in memory that can't be wiped."
applyTo: "**/*.cs"
---

# Allocations and buffers

<!-- Generated by `npm run train` from the sources each rule cites. To change a rule for good, change its source or say so in training/feedback.md; the next training run regenerates this file. -->

- **Hold secret material in sensitive pooled rentals that are pinned and zeroed on return, such as `BufferFactory.Rent(..., isSensitive: true, ...)` or `SecureMemoryPool` from `NCode.Buffers`, and dispose each rental as soon as the operation that needs it finishes. Secret material includes passwords and their decoded or normalized forms, private keys and PEM text, content-encryption and key-encryption keys, shared secrets and decrypted plaintext. Never keep it in a `string`, a plain or `ArrayPool` array, a pinned GC array wiped by hand, or a non-sensitive rental or writer. This includes the fallback used when the data is too large for `stackalloc`.** A string can't be zeroed and the GC may copy it. A plain or non-sensitive buffer leaves the secret on the heap or in a shared pool, and a hand-wiped pinned array keeps it outside the secure pool and depends on a manual `ZeroMemory` call that can be missed. *Check:* Flag secret bytes or text held in `new byte[]`, `GC.AllocateArray`/`GC.AllocateUninitializedArray(..., pinned: true)`, `ArrayPool<T>` rentals, `Encoding.GetBytes(string)` results, `File.ReadAllText`/`ReadAllBytes` of key files, strings, or rentals with `isSensitive: false`. Also flag secret rentals that are kept past the hash, sign, verify or unwrap call, and secret-holding buffers returned to a pool without being cleared. <sub>Identity ADR-1230; Identity ADR-1235; Identity ADR-1238; Identity ADR-1409; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity review of #420; Identity outcomes of #532</sub>
- **When a method writes output whose length the caller can't know in advance, such as an unwrapped or decrypted key whose size only a remote service's response reveals, take an `IBufferWriter<byte>` destination. Don't take a fixed `Span<byte>`/`Memory<byte>` and return a byte count. Call `Advance` only after the operation succeeds, and zero anything already written to the writer if it fails. Keep `Span<byte>` plus `out int` for results of known size.** With a fixed destination, callers have to guess the size, for example by renting twice the expected length. A result of the wrong length then fails as "destination too small" instead of reaching the caller's own size check. A partial or failed write must not leave secret bytes in the writer. *Check:* Look at unwrap, decrypt and remote-service methods. Flag ones that return a fresh `byte[]`, take a fixed span or memory for a variable-length result, call `Advance` before success, or leave written bytes uncleared on an exception path. Also flag callers that over-rent buffers to work around a fixed destination. <sub>Identity ADR-1260; Identity review of #370</sub>
- **Read a response body from an untrusted endpoint only after sending with `HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead`, and only through a reader that enforces a hard byte cap while streaming into a pooled `IBufferWriter<byte>`. Treat `Content-Length` only as a hint. Parse the capped body directly from the written buffer sequence.** Pipeline timeouts end when the headers arrive, so an uncapped body read can exhaust resources. A missing or false `Content-Length` must not bypass the cap, and copying the body into an intermediate array or string defeats the pooled design. *Check:* Flag `ReadAsStringAsync`, `ReadAsByteArrayAsync`, `ReadFromJsonAsync` or `ReadAsStreamAsync` copies on untrusted responses, caps that trust `Content-Length`, and `.ToArray()`, `Encoding.GetString` or `MemoryStream` copies of the written sequence before it is parsed. <sub>Identity ADR-1315</sub>
- **When you pre-size a collection or buffer from a length read out of peer-supplied data, such as a CBOR array or map header or a length prefix, clamp the capacity to what the remaining input bytes could actually hold.** The declared count is controlled by the attacker. An unclamped capacity such as 2^31-1 lets a tiny message force a huge allocation. *Check:* Look for `new List<T>(n)`, `new Dictionary<K,V>(n)` or buffer rentals where `n` comes from a decoded header. Check that `n` is bounded by the remaining bytes (half of them for maps) and that a test feeds an oversized declared length. <sub>Identity outcomes of #554</sub>
- **Split a fixed-segment string with `MemoryExtensions.Split` into a `stackalloc Range[expected + 1]` and reject any segment count other than `expected`.** Without the spare slot, extra segments fold into the last range and pass validation. `string.Split` also allocates. *Check:* Flag `string.Split` on fixed-format input, and `Range` buffers sized exactly to the expected count. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **An in-process store that keeps caller-supplied bytes must copy them on write. A write API that copies the value before its task completes must document that guarantee on its interface, so callers can return their pooled rental as soon as the call finishes.** If the store keeps the caller's memory, a caller that reuses or returns its buffer can change an entry that is already stored. Callers can safely pass pooled buffers only when the copy is guaranteed. *Check:* Flag store implementations that save a `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>` or array argument without copying it. Also flag rented memory passed to async store writes whose interface doesn't document the copy. <sub>Identity ADR-1164; Identity review of #420</sub>
- **Don't report a `ToArray()` copy of caller-supplied memory that is passed to a client command which can be abandoned, for example through `WaitAsync` or cancellation, while the client may still send it later.** An abandoned command may be sent after the caller's buffer has been returned or reused, so the adapter has to pass an array it owns. *Check:* Before flagging the allocation, look for a comment explaining the copy, for abandonment through `WaitAsync` or cancellation, and for sibling methods in the adapter that also pass arrays they own. <sub>Identity outcomes of #460</sub>
- **In production code, copy every collection a type stores, including an injected `IEnumerable<T>`, once into a collection it owns before assigning it to a field or property. Choose the type by how it is used: `FrozenDictionary`/`FrozenSet` for repeated lookups, `ImmutableArray<T>` or an array (`.ToArray()`, `[.. x]`) for iteration, and `List<T>` only for a genuinely mutable working set.** A stored caller collection can change underneath the type, and a lazy sequence is enumerated again on each use. *Check:* Flag constructors, setters or methods that assign a collection or `IEnumerable<T>` parameter directly to a member. *Note:* Test projects are exempt, for example a private sealed nested stub that one test file needs. <sub>Identity convention-audit.instructions.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **In production code, dispose every `HttpResponseMessage`, `Stream` and `IHttpClientFactory`-created `HttpClient` the code owns. This includes each response that a retry discards, which must be disposed before the next attempt is sent.** Undisposed responses, streams and clients hold their connections and buffers. In retry loops this can exhaust connections. *Check:* Flag results of `SendAsync`/`GetAsync`, opened streams and factory-created clients that have no `using`/`Dispose`. Also flag retry logic or `OnRetry` callbacks that drop the previous response without disposing it. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity ADR-1336</sub>
- **Dispose a disposable client, credential or certificate that a cache drops, whether it lost a `GetOrAdd` creation race or was evicted, removed or released. Never dispose one while a call, handler or handshake may still be using it: keep such objects in a singleton cache that disposes them when the container is disposed.** Dropped clients that own channels, HTTP clients or refreshing credentials hold sockets until finalization. Disposing a certificate under a live handler breaks its handshakes. *Check:* Look at `GetOrAdd` races, `TryRemove`, eviction and release paths on caches of disposable objects. Flag a losing or removed instance that is never disposed, and an object disposed in a `using` block, or evicted, while a handler or in-flight call still holds it. <sub>Identity outcomes of #584; Identity ADR-1300</sub>
- **Don't ask a component to dispose a replaced cached certificate collection on rotation when operations in flight on other threads may still be using the old one and nothing counts references to it.** Disposing on rotation would break a chain build in flight on another request. The certificates hold nothing their finalizers don't release, and rotation is rare. *Check:* Before reporting a leaked cached `X509Certificate2Collection` on reload, check whether concurrent readers can still hold the old reference. <sub>Identity outcomes of #794</sub>
- **Resolve a request's client certificate once and cache it in `HttpContext.Items`, so that every consumer, such as client authentication and token binding, sees the same certificate. Dispose the certificates you decoded, for example from a forwarded header, when the request ends, and never dispose `HttpContext.Connection.ClientCertificate`.** All consumers must agree on one certificate. Decoded certificates belong to the request, but the connection's certificate belongs to the connection. *Check:* Flag repeated decoding of the certificate header for each consumer, decoded `X509Certificate2` instances that are never disposed or registered for disposal with the response, and any disposal of `Connection.ClientCertificate`. <sub>Identity ADR-1172</sub>
- **In production code, when an implementation writes characters inside a `string.Create` callback, verify that the writer's `WrittenCount` equals `chars.Length`, and pass span inputs through an `internal readonly ref struct` state.** The check keeps a `'\0'` remainder from ever being persisted, and ref-struct state avoids copying the inputs. *Check:* Flag `string.Create` callbacks that delegate writing but don't verify the written count. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **When data built in a span has to survive an `await`, hold it in a pooled `Memory<byte>` rental that lives across the await and is returned in a `using` or `finally` once the awaited call completes. Don't copy it to a transient array with `ToArray()`, and don't restructure the code to try to keep a span alive across the await.** A span can't be held across an `await`. One pooled copy per operation keeps the asynchronous path free of avoidable heap allocations. *Check:* In async methods, flag `lease.Span.ToArray()` or `.Memory.ToArray()` results that are only passed to an awaited call, and pooled buffers used across an await that aren't returned after it. <sub>Identity ADR-1472; Identity outcomes of #702</sub>
- **In production code, a method that produces binary output, whether crypto, encoding, serialization or key material, writes into a destination the caller supplies: a `ref TWriter` (`where TWriter : IBufferWriter<byte>, allows ref struct`), an `IBufferWriter<byte>`, a `Utf8JsonWriter`, or a `Span<byte>`/`Memory<byte>` with a companion method that returns the required length. It takes `ReadOnlySpan<byte>`/`ReadOnlyMemory<byte>` inputs. It doesn't return or take `byte[]`. Async remote operations, such as sign, decrypt and key agreement against a key service, write into a caller-supplied `Memory<byte>` and return `ValueTask<int>`.** Returning arrays allocates on every call and forces the caller to copy. A caller-supplied destination lets the caller choose a pooled, stack or sensitive buffer. *Check:* Flag new protect, encrypt, encode, sign or serialize methods that return `byte[]` or `Task<byte[]>`, for example `SerializeToUtf8Bytes` or `ToArray()` results, and new methods that take `byte[]` parameters for binary data. *Note:* See the rule that exempts non-secret wire encoders whose array return is recorded in an ADR. <sub>Identity ADR-1235; Identity ADR-1474; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity review of #382; Identity review of #420</sub>
- **Don't ask a token or message encoder that returns a new `byte[]` to write into a caller-supplied buffer writer instead when its output is non-secret wire data that the caller keeps or sends whole, and an ADR records that array-returning design.** Such an encoder returns the whole message as an array, just as a compact token is returned as a string. A pooled or sensitive destination adds nothing for non-secret output. *Check:* Before asking for buffer-writer or `ref TWriter` overloads on an encode or issue API, check whether the output is secret, and whether sibling encoders or an ADR establish the array-return convention. <sub>Identity outcomes of #554</sub>
- **In production code, use a pooled rental from `NCode.Buffers` (`BufferFactory.Rent`, or `BufferFactory.CreatePooledBufferWriter` inside a `using`) or a small fixed `stackalloc` for a transient buffer, including scratch space between writing serialized data and reading it back. Use `new byte[]`, `.ToArray()`, `ArrayBufferWriter<T>`, `MemoryStream`, `JsonSerializer.SerializeToUtf8Bytes` or `Encoding.GetBytes(string)` only where an external API requires them, and over a rented array obtained with `MemoryMarshal.TryGetArray` where possible.** A transient bare array is an avoidable heap allocation on every call, and it can't be pinned or reliably zeroed. *Check:* Flag local, short-lived `new byte[n]` (especially when `n` is a known constant or comes from an algorithm descriptor), `GC.AllocateArray`, `ArrayBufferWriter<byte>`, `MemoryStream`, `SerializeToUtf8Bytes` or `GetBytes(string)` buffers that are neither returned nor stored and that no external API requires. <sub>Identity ADR-1235; Identity ADR-1283; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity review of #316; Identity review of #382; Identity review of #420</sub>
- **Don't flag a single exactly sized array allocation when an object owns the array and it outlives the call. Pooling applies only to buffers that live for the duration of the call.** A rented buffer can't be stored in an object that outlives the call, so one exact allocation is intentional there. *Check:* Before reporting an allocation, check whether the array is assigned to a field or property of a returned or stored object. <sub>Identity review of #420</sub>
- **Don't ask for a value that isn't a credential, such as a lease-ownership nonce, to be encoded into a rented, zeroed buffer when the same bytes are already stored elsewhere in plaintext, or when the code receiving them copies them into an array it owns.** Renting and zeroing such a value removes no copy of it and keeps a rental alive for the whole operation, so it gains no secrecy. *Check:* Before reporting an unpooled or unzeroed encoding, confirm the value is actually secret and check whether it is stored or copied elsewhere. <sub>Identity outcomes of #460</sub>
- **Read a multi-segment `Sequence<T>` or `ReadOnlySequence<T>` segment by segment or with `SequenceReader<byte>`. When a consumer needs one contiguous span, such as a cryptographic primitive or a base64url codec, take `GetSpanLease(isSensitive:)` from `NCode.Buffers`. Never use `.ToArray()` or concatenate segments by hand.** The lease returns the single segment without copying, or otherwise a pooled copy with the right sensitivity. Other copies allocate and may leave secret copies behind. *Check:* Flag `ReadOnlySequence<byte>.ToArray()`, loops that copy segments into a new array, and contiguous consumers that don't use `GetSpanLease`. <sub>Identity ADR-1266; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Use a `BufferFactory.Rent` (`NCode.Buffers`) out-buffer at its returned length, which is exactly the requested length whether `isSensitive` is true or false, without slicing it back. Don't report a missing `[..length]` slice on such a buffer. In production code, prefer the `out Span<T>` overload, and take `out Memory<T>` only for a buffer stored in a field or used across an `await`.** Unlike raw `ArrayPool<T>`/`MemoryPool<T>` rentals, `BufferFactory.Rent` doesn't return oversized buffers. A span is cheaper when memory isn't needed. *Check:* Flag a `.Slice(0, length)`/`[..length]` added to a `BufferFactory.Rent` result, and `out Memory<T>` used only synchronously within one method. Only ask for a slice when the buffer came from `ArrayPool<T>.Rent` or `MemoryPool<T>.Rent`. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity outcomes of #807</sub>
- **In production code, a helper that rents and fills a buffer for its caller returns the lease together with a read-only view (`out ReadOnlySpan<T>`, or `out ReadOnlyMemory<T>` when it is used across an `await`), not a writable one.** Only the rent call itself should hand back writable memory. Consumers shouldn't mutate output that has already been filled. *Check:* Flag helpers that return a lease with `out Span<T>`/`out Memory<T>` over already-filled data. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Create a `string` only for a non-secret value at a storage or wire boundary, and create it exactly once, in place, with `string.Create`. Don't fill a rented `char` buffer and then copy it out with `new string(span)` or `AsSpan().ToString()`.** The copy is a needless extra allocation and pass. Secret values must not become strings at all. *Check:* Flag `ArrayPool<char>` rentals followed by `new string(...)` or `.ToString()`, intermediate strings on hot paths, and strings created from secret or plaintext payload bytes. <sub>Identity ADR-1235; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Parse and validate text with `ReadOnlySpan<char>` slices, `MemoryExtensions.Split` ranges and span `StartsWith`/`Equals`. A method that only reads a text input, and doesn't store it, takes `ReadOnlySpan<char>` instead of `string`. Properties on public request or contract types stay `string`.** Span slicing doesn't allocate substrings or arrays. A `string` converts implicitly to `ReadOnlySpan<char>`, so existing callers still compile and can pass slices. *Check:* Flag `.Split(`, `.Substring(` or private helpers that return string slices in parsing or validation code. Also flag new or changed helper methods with `string` parameters that are only read, encoded or hashed, unless they are properties of a public contract type. <sub>Identity review of #420; Identity review of #341</sub>
- **Encode short or composed non-secret text into a `stackalloc` or rented span with `Encoding.GetBytes(ReadOnlySpan<char>, Span<byte>)`, or append its parts to an `IncrementalHash`. Hash into a `stackalloc` span with the `HashData(source, destination)` overloads. Don't use the array-returning overloads, and don't use the secure encoding helpers for text that isn't sensitive.** Interpolating a string and calling `GetBytes` allocates a string and an array just to hash them. The secure encoding is meant for sensitive text. *Check:* Flag `GetBytes(string)`, `SecureEncoding.*.GetBytes` on an interpolated non-secret string, and `SHA256.HashData(bytes)` results that are used once and then dropped. <sub>Identity review of #420; Identity outcomes of #692</sub>
- **Expose a fixed byte label that is used on every call as a `static ReadOnlySpan<byte> Label => "..."u8;` property, not as a `const string` encoded on each call.** Encoding a constant string on every call allocates and repeats work. *Check:* Flag a `const string` passed through `Encoding.*.GetBytes` on a hot path. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **Back an immutable JSON-wrapping type or a read-back record with a detached `JsonElement` (for example from `JsonElement.Parse`) that owns no `JsonDocument`, and write JSON records into a pooled buffer writer.** A detached element leaves nothing to dispose or defensively clone, and the pooled writer avoids allocating a `byte[]`. *Check:* Flag wrapper types that hold a `JsonDocument`, implement `IDisposable` only to free one, or clone on every access. Also flag `JsonDocument.Parse` used to read back a record, and `ToArray()`/`MemoryStream` in record serialization. <sub>Identity ADR-1119; Identity ADR-1283</sub>
- **Pass array-backed `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>` to an SDK that takes arrays through `MemoryMarshal.TryGetArray` without copying it. Copy only when the SDK needs an array of exactly the data's length.** This avoids a needless copy on every call. *Check:* Flag `ToArray()` on a `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>` handed to an SDK where `TryGetArray` would provide the segment directly. <sub>Identity ADR-1474</sub>
- **Read and write a defined little-endian wire encoding with `BinaryPrimitives`, not by reinterpreting memory. Use `MemoryMarshal.Cast<byte, T>` only for byte-aligned limb radixes (for example, not radix-2^51). When you view a struct of a single blittable field type as a span with `MemoryMarshal.CreateSpan(ref Unsafe.As<TStruct, TField>(ref value), count)`, cover it with round-trip tests that verify its sequential layout.** Reinterpreting memory depends on host endianness and matches the wire format only for byte-aligned limbs. A struct span view relies on a layout that only tests verify. *Check:* Flag `MemoryMarshal.Cast`/`Unsafe.As` used to serialize wire data or non-byte-aligned limbs, and new struct span views that have no round-trip test. <sub>Identity ADR-1266</sub>
- **Convert a DER-encoded ECDSA signature to fixed-width r‖s, with each half `(KeySizeBits + 7) / 8` bytes, using a strict parser built on `AsnDecoder`. Hash the signing input into a rental whose `isSensitive` is given explicitly.** Strict parsing rejects malformed signatures, a wrong half width produces invalid signatures, and a rented digest keeps signing off the allocation path. *Check:* Flag hand-rolled or lenient DER parsing, a wrong half width, and a digest allocated as a new array or rented without an explicit `isSensitive`. <sub>Identity ADR-1474</sub>
- **Size a collection when its count is known, return a shared empty instance (`[]`, `FrozenSet<T>.Empty`), create collections that are often empty lazily, and write `list ?? (IReadOnlyCollection<T>)[]` rather than `list ?? []`.** `list ?? []` on a `List<T>`-typed expression allocates a new list, and unsized collections reallocate as they grow. *Check:* Flag `new List<T>()` without a capacity when the count is known, `?? []` on a `List<T>`-typed expression, and eagerly created collections that usually stay empty. *Note:* When the count comes from peer-supplied data, clamp it as the rule on peer-supplied lengths requires. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **Choose between a stack buffer and a rented buffer in one conditional expression, and dispose the optional lease with a `using` declaration. Don't declare a placeholder such as `stackalloc byte[0]` just to satisfy an analyzer, and don't use a nullable lease local disposed in `try`/`finally`.** A placeholder and a hand-written try/finally are harder to read and depart from the house disposal style. *Check:* Flag `stackalloc byte[0]` that is later overwritten, analyzer suppressions next to it, and nullable lease locals disposed in `finally`. <sub>Identity outcomes of #552</sub>
- **Don't ask for a literal initial capacity passed to a growable pooled buffer writer, such as `BufferFactory.CreatePooledBufferWriter`, to become a named constant.** The value is only a starting capacity that the writer grows past, not a limit. *Check:* Before reporting a magic number, check whether it is the initial-capacity argument of a growable buffer rather than a limit. <sub>Identity outcomes of #709</sub>
- **In production code, buffer data by default and add streaming APIs such as `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` only for a stated need.** Buffered data is simpler to own, copy and dispose correctly. Streaming should be a deliberate choice. *Check:* Flag new streaming APIs or `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` returns that have no stated reason. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **In production code, model a small immutable value, such as a key, descriptor, command or disposition value, as a `readonly record struct`.** A readonly record struct avoids a heap allocation for each value and provides value equality. *Check:* Flag small immutable values modeled as classes or mutable structs. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
